title: Stabilizing Causal Structure Learning under Heteroscedasticity: Analysis and Mitigation of Optimization Failures

problem.claim: The study addresses causal DAG learning under heteroscedastic noise models.

gap.claim: Although heteroscedastic noise models theoretically identify causal structures, gradient-based continuous DAG learning can fail because likelihood optimization interacts adversely with the acyclicity constraint.

contributions.claim: The work identifies and formalizes an optimization failure mode caused by early attenuation of the reconstruction gradient and dominance of the acyclicity constraint.
It proposes a graduated optimization strategy using a surrogate loss that decouples the variance term from reconstruction loss.
It introduces a scheduling coefficient that transitions optimization from stable mean learning toward full heteroscedastic likelihood optimization and acyclicity enforcement.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the strategy avoids the identified failure mode and produces DAGs that better reflect the data.
The authors report effectiveness on synthetic and real-world datasets.
The authors provide a GitHub repository containing code and supplementary material.

narrative_sequence.summary: The study considers causal DAG learning with heteroscedastic noise.
Continuous gradient-based DAG learning may fail despite theoretical identifiability.
Early variance-dependent gradient attenuation can let the acyclicity constraint dominate parameter updates.
The work formalizes the failure and proposes graduated optimization with a surrogate loss and scheduling coefficient.
The authors report improved data-reflecting DAGs and effectiveness on synthetic and real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Optimization objectives can produce ineffective structure learning when a constraint dominates before the data-fitting signal is learned.

interpretation.claim: Constraint scheduling may be important when objective components have imbalanced early-training gradients.

application.claim: For constrained heteroscedastic structure learning, consider staged optimization that first stabilizes mean reconstruction and later emphasizes variance modeling and constraint enforcement.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this scheduling principle generalizes beyond the studied heteroscedastic DAG-learning setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not report quantitative results, evaluation metrics, baselines, or dataset sizes.
The abstract does not specify the formal assumptions, optimization details, or limitations of the proposed strategy.
